note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Protocol-space inconsistency problem to causal two-stage CauseCollab design and its empirical support

nodes.name: Heterogeneous agents hinder feature fusion
nodes.description: In real deployments collaborative agents come from different manufacturers and platforms, with differing sensor types, voxel sizes and network architectures, which makes intermediate features hard to fuse.

nodes.name: Pairwise mapping scales poorly
nodes.description: One-stage methods learn a dedicated mapping for each pair of heterogeneous modalities, so training cost grows rapidly with the number of modalities.

nodes.name: Protocol-space methods scale better
nodes.description: Two-stage methods map each modality into a shared protocol space with a per-modality converter and reconstructor, improving scalability.

nodes.name: Independent converters yield pseudo-protocol distributions
nodes.description: Training converters independently per modality makes each learn a locally self-consistent mapping, producing inconsistent pseudo-protocol distributions, semantic and statistical discrepancies across modalities, and error accumulation, especially when the modality gap is large.

nodes.name: Root cause: protocol space as mere alignment intermediary
nodes.description: Existing methods model the protocol space only as a distribution-alignment intermediary and do not characterize which semantic factors are shared and which modality-specific statistical confounders should be suppressed.

nodes.name: Causal model treats noise as confounders
nodes.description: A structural causal model treats the true semantic factor S as the causal factor and the protocol and heterogeneous-modality statistical noises Np and Nm as confounders that create spurious correlation paths and modality-specific semantic clusters.

nodes.name: Causal metric learning with MGI-SPD
nodes.description: Counterfactual intervention via causal metric learning, implemented by the Mask-Guided Intervention via SPD Feature Geometry module, drives each modality's protocol representation toward the weakly observed protocol modality, suppressing pseudo-protocol shifts.

nodes.name: Unified converter with SCE and CGDR
nodes.description: A unified converter combining a semantic context extractor and a context-guided dynamic refiner is trained on multi-modality mixed batches, using global semantics as an anchor to constrain local refinement and reduce background-induced misalignment.

nodes.name: Stage-2 local reconstruction
nodes.description: With the Stage-1 converter frozen, a ConvNeXt-based local semantic reconstructor is trained for each modality to restore protocol features to that modality's local space.

nodes.name: Adapters add new modalities cheaply
nodes.description: For a new modality the converter backbone is frozen and only low-rank bottleneck adapters (initialized with scaling coefficient 0) are trained to align it to the protocol space, plus a local reconstructor.

nodes.name: Best OPV2V results as agents added
nodes.description: On OPV2V with Lpp4 ego and three heterogeneous neighbors added progressively, CauseCollab achieves the best AP@0.3 and AP@0.5 against MPDA, HEAL, PnPDA and STAMP.

nodes.name: Gains in large modality gap
nodes.description: With a larger modality gap, CauseCollab improves AP by 4.2% at IoU 0.3 and 3.6% at IoU 0.5 for ego CEff and neighbor CRes, and by 0.5%/0.4% for ego Lpp4 and neighbor CEff.

nodes.name: Outperforms on real-world DAIR-V2X
nodes.description: On DAIR-V2X, with Lpp4 and CEff as ego, CauseCollab outperforms all previous methods overall.

nodes.name: Novel modalities with fewer trainable parameters
nodes.description: Adapting to novel modalities Lsd2 and CEffB1 gives higher average precision with fewer trainable parameters, indicating semantic consistency and parameter reuse.

nodes.name: Causal intervention ablation
nodes.description: Removing the causal intervention module significantly lowers AP at IoU 0.3 and 0.5, and removing the intervention mask also degrades performance.

nodes.name: Converter component ablations
nodes.description: Removing semantic context guidance causes a substantial drop, replacing CGDR or SCE+CGDR with a single-tower ConvNeXt degrades further, and removing the new-modality adapter also degrades performance.

nodes.name: Cleaner protocol features than STAMP
nodes.description: Visualization shows a semantic gap between LiDAR and camera intermediate features; STAMP's protocol features from camera contain semantically irrelevant background noise while CauseCollab's are cleaner and more cross-modally consistent.

isolated_nodes.name: Robust to localization noise
isolated_nodes.description: CauseCollab's performance remains robust under Gaussian pose noise with standard deviation from 0.0 to 0.5 (Fig 3).

isolated_nodes.name: Large modality gap makes pseudo-protocols worse
isolated_nodes.description: The inconsistency of pseudo-protocol distributions becomes particularly pronounced when the modality gap is large, introducing noisy responses and spurious activations in background regions.

structural_reasoning: A chain from heterogeneity and scalability limitations of prior methods, through the protocol-space inconsistency diagnosis, to the causal and converter design and then to experimental validation; robustness analyses isolated.
